title: Product of square roots
useWhen: Two square roots to multiply, or a product to write as a single root.

title: Quotient of square roots
useWhen: A quotient of square roots, or a root of a fraction to split.

title: Square root of a square
useWhen: A square root of a square, and the inside may be negative.

title: Rationalise a single surd
useWhen: A single square root sitting in a denominator.

title: Rationalise a binomial surd
useWhen: A denominator that is an integer plus or minus a square root.

title: Product of powers
useWhen: Powers of the same base to multiply, or a product to turn into one power.

title: Power of a power
useWhen: A power already raised to another power, to collapse into one index.

title: Negative index
useWhen: A negative index to rewrite as a reciprocal, or the reverse.

title: Direct proportion
useWhen: Two quantities that stay in a constant ratio.

title: Inverse proportion
useWhen: Two quantities whose product stays constant as one grows and the other shrinks.

title: Equation of a line
useWhen: A straight line when you know the gradient and the y-intercept.

title: Linear function
useWhen: A graph or mapping that is a straight line through a given slope.

title: General equation of a line
useWhen: A line given as ax + by + c = 0, not in slope form.

title: Square of a binomial
useWhen: A sum or difference to square without expanding the long way.

title: Difference of squares
useWhen: A difference of two squares to factor, or a product of conjugates.

title: Binomial expansion
useWhen: A binomial raised to a small whole-number power.

title: Power function
useWhen: A model or graph of the form y = k x^n.

title: Pythagoras
useWhen: A right-angled triangle when you know two sides and need the third.

title: Sine, cosine, tangent
useWhen: A right-angled triangle: opposite, adjacent or hypotenuse with an acute angle.

variables.meaning: Acute angle in a right-angled triangle

title: Tangent from sine and cosine
useWhen: You already have sine and cosine of the same angle and need tangent.

title: Circumference of a circle
useWhen: Distance around a circle from its radius or diameter.

title: Area of a circle
useWhen: The area inside a full circle, from its radius.

title: Arc length (degrees)
useWhen: A circular arc when the angle is given in degrees.

title: Sector area (degrees)
useWhen: A pizza-slice of a circle when the angle is in degrees.

title: Intercept theorem
useWhen: Parallel lines cutting two rays, and you need matching length ratios.

variables.meaning: Line parallel to side BC, cutting AB and AC

title: Position vector
useWhen: A point given from the origin as a vector.

title: Parallelogram formula
useWhen: The diagonal of a parallelogram built from two vectors.

variables.meaning: Vertices; ABCD is a parallelogram when either equality holds

title: Rational index as a radical
useWhen: A fractional index to write as a root, or a root to write as a power.

title: Three forms of a quadratic
useWhen: A quadratic to rewrite between expanded, factorised and completed-square form.

title: Quadratic formula
useWhen: A quadratic that will not factor, or you need exact roots.

variables.meaning: Coefficients in ax² + bx + c = 0, a ≠ 0

title: Discriminant
useWhen: How many real roots a quadratic has, before solving it.

variables.meaning: > 0 two real roots, = 0 one root, < 0 none over the reals

title: Axis and vertex of a parabola
useWhen: The turning point or axis of symmetry of y = ax^2 + bx + c.

title: Standard exponential model
useWhen: Growth or decay of the form y = k a^x.

variables.meaning: Growth factor: a > 1 growth, 0 < a < 1 decay

title: Definition of a logarithm
useWhen: Changing between b^x = a and a logarithm, or the reverse.

title: Logarithm of a product
useWhen: A log of a product to split, or a sum of logs of the same base.

title: Logarithm of a quotient
useWhen: A log of a quotient to split, or a difference of logs of the same base.

title: Logarithm of a power
useWhen: A log of a power, or a coefficient in front of a log to move.

title: Sine, cosine, tangent on the reals
katex: y = \sin x,\quad y = \cos x,\quad y = \tan x
useWhen: Sine, cosine or tangent of any real angle, not only an acute one.

variables.meaning: Real number (radians in later work; degrees still used)

title: Transformed sine
useWhen: A sine graph that has been stretched, shifted or both.

title: Degrees to radians
useWhen: An angle to convert between degrees and radians.

variables.meaning: The same angle in both units

title: Complementary angles
useWhen: Two angles that add to 90°, and you need sine or cosine of one from the other.

title: Supplementary angles
useWhen: Two angles that add to 180°, and you need sine of one from the other.

title: Pythagorean identity
useWhen: You know sin or cos of an angle and need the other, without a triangle.

title: Cosine of a sum or difference
useWhen: Cosine of a sum or difference of two angles.

title: Sine of a sum or difference
useWhen: Sine of a sum or difference of two angles.

title: Double-angle sine
useWhen: Sine of twice an angle, from sin and cos of the single angle.

title: Double-angle cosine
useWhen: Cosine of twice an angle, from sin or cos of the single angle.

title: Cosine rule
useWhen: A triangle with two sides and the included angle, or all three sides.

title: Sine rule
useWhen: A triangle with a side and its opposite angle, plus one more piece.

variables.meaning: Sides opposite angles α, β, γ

title: Area of a triangle (SAS)
useWhen: Area of a triangle from two sides and the included angle.

variables.meaning: Included angle between sides b and c

title: Magnitude of a vector
useWhen: The length of a vector from its components.

title: Scalar product from an angle
useWhen: The angle between two vectors, or a projection, from their lengths.

title: Distance between two points
useWhen: The distance between two points given by coordinates.

title: Scalar product in an orthonormal basis
useWhen: A dot product from components in an orthonormal basis.

title: Probability bounds
useWhen: A probability that must lie between 0 and 1.

title: Complementary event
useWhen: The chance that an event does not happen.

title: Addition rule
useWhen: The chance of A or B when the events may overlap.

title: Mutually exclusive addition
useWhen: The chance of A or B when the events cannot happen together.

title: Conditional probability
useWhen: The chance of A given that B has already happened.

title: Independent events
useWhen: Two events that do not affect each other, and you need P(A and B).

title: Standard deviation
useWhen: Spread of a data set when you already have the mean.

title: Standard deviation (raw scores)
useWhen: Spread of a data set from the raw scores, without listing deviations.

title: Complex number
useWhen: A complex number written as a + bi.

title: Explicit sequence
useWhen: The nth term given directly as a formula in n.

title: Recursive sequence
useWhen: A term defined from the previous one, plus a starting value.

title: Derivative at a point
useWhen: The gradient of a curve at a point from first principles.

title: Power rule
useWhen: The derivative of x^n, or a polynomial term by term.

variables.meaning: Real exponent (x > 0 when n is not an integer)

title: Second derivative
useWhen: Concavity, or whether a stationary point is a max or min.

variables.meaning: Rate of change of the gradient

title: Tangent to a graph
useWhen: The equation of the tangent to y = f(x) at a given point.

title: Exponential of base e
useWhen: Growth or decay with base e, or the derivative of e^x.

title: Natural logarithm
useWhen: The inverse of e^x, or a log with base e.

title: Index and logarithm rules
useWhen: Switching between index form and log form, or simplifying mixed logs.

title: Vector equation of a line
useWhen: A line in the plane given by a point and a direction vector.

title: Equation of a circle
useWhen: A circle from its centre and radius, or to read those from the equation.

title: Angle between two lines
useWhen: The angle between two lines from their gradients or direction vectors.

title: Distance from a point to a line
useWhen: The shortest distance from a point to a line ax + by + c = 0.

title: Permutations of n objects
useWhen: The number of ways to arrange n distinct objects.

title: Permutations of k from n
useWhen: Ordered selections of k objects from n, without repetition.

title: Permutations with repetition
useWhen: Ordered selections of k from n when objects may be repeated.

title: Combinations
useWhen: Unordered selections of k objects from n, without repetition.

title: Combinations with repetition
useWhen: Unordered selections of k from n when objects may be repeated.

title: Binomial identities
useWhen: A binomial-coefficient identity, or a Pascal-triangle relation to prove.

title: Total probability
useWhen: P(A) by splitting into cases that partition the sample space.

variables.meaning: A partition of the sample space

title: Bayes' theorem
useWhen: You know P(B|A) and need the reverse, P(A|B).

title: Expected value (discrete)
useWhen: The long-run average of a discrete random variable.

title: Variance (discrete)
useWhen: The spread of a discrete random variable about its mean.

title: Binomial probability
useWhen: A fixed number of independent yes/no trials, same probability each time.

title: Binomial mean and variance
useWhen: Mean or variance of a binomial count, without listing every outcome.

title: Modulus of a complex number
useWhen: The distance of a complex number from the origin.

title: Argument of a complex number
useWhen: The angle a complex number makes with the positive real axis.

title: Exponential form
useWhen: A complex number in modulus-argument form, or multiplying by rotating.

title: nth roots of a complex number
useWhen: The n distinct nth roots of a complex number.

title: Arithmetic sequence — nth term
useWhen: The nth term of a sequence with a constant difference.

title: Geometric sequence — nth term
useWhen: The nth term of a sequence with a constant ratio.

title: Sum of an arithmetic sequence
useWhen: The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic sequence.

title: Sum of a geometric sequence
useWhen: The sum of the first n terms of a geometric sequence.

title: Oblique asymptote
useWhen: A slanted asymptote of a rational function, not a horizontal one.

variables.meaning: The oblique asymptote when both limits exist

title: Definite integral
useWhen: Net signed area under a curve between two x-values.

title: Linearity of the integral
useWhen: An integral of a sum or scalar multiple, to split or factor.

title: Additivity of interval
useWhen: An integral split at an interior point, or two adjacent intervals joined.

title: Volume of revolution
useWhen: The volume of a solid made by rotating a curve about the x-axis.

variables.meaning: Rotated about the x-axis from a to b

title: Line in 3D
useWhen: A line in space from a point and a direction vector.

title: Vector product
katex: \vec{u}\times\vec{v} = \begin{vmatrix} \mathbf{i} & \mathbf{j} & \mathbf{k} \\ u_{x} & u_{y} & u_{z} \\ v_{x} & v_{y} & v_{z} \end{vmatrix}
useWhen: A vector perpendicular to two given vectors, or the area of the parallelogram.

title: Cartesian equation of a plane
useWhen: A plane as ax + by + cz + d = 0, and you need a normal.

title: Vector equation of a plane
useWhen: A plane from a point and two non-parallel directions in it.

variables.meaning: Two non-parallel directions in the plane

title: Distance from a point to a plane
useWhen: The shortest distance from a point to a plane.

title: Angle between two planes
useWhen: The angle between two planes, from their normals.

title: Pearson correlation
useWhen: How strongly two numerical variables follow a straight line.

variables.meaning: In [-1, 1]; sign is the direction, size is the strength

title: Least-squares regression
useWhen: The straight line of best fit for predicting y from x.

variables.meaning: Gradient of the regression of y on x

title: Expected value (continuous)
useWhen: The mean of a continuous random variable from its density.

title: Normal density
useWhen: A bell-shaped continuous model with a given mean and spread.

title: Standardisation
useWhen: A normal value to convert into a z-score, or the reverse.

variables.meaning: Standard normal when X is N(μ, σ²)

title: Euclidean division
useWhen: Dividing integers with a remainder strictly smaller than the divisor.

title: Bézout's identity
useWhen: Writing gcd(a, b) as an integer combination of a and b.

title: Bachet–Bézout theorem
useWhen: Whether ax + by = 1 has integer solutions, i.e. whether a and b are coprime.

title: Fermat's little theorem
useWhen: A power modulo a prime that does not divide the base.

title: Product of matrices
useWhen: The product of two matrices whose inner sizes match.

title: Inverse of a 2×2 matrix
katex: \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{ad-bc}\begin{pmatrix} d & -b \\ -c & a \end{pmatrix}
useWhen: The inverse of a 2×2 matrix with non-zero determinant.

title: Derivative of an inverse
useWhen: The gradient of an inverse function at a point.

variables.meaning: Differentiable and invertible near the point

title: Mean value theorem
useWhen: A point where the instantaneous gradient equals the chord from a to b.

title: 2×2 determinant
katex: \det\begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix} = ad - bc
useWhen: The determinant of a 2×2 matrix, or whether it is invertible.

title: Cofactor expansion
useWhen: The determinant of a larger matrix, expanded along a row or column.

title: Inverse from the adjugate
useWhen: The inverse of an n×n matrix from det A and the adjugate.

title: Rouché–Fröbenius
katex: Ax = b\text{ is consistent} \iff \operatorname{rank} A = \operatorname{rank}[A \mid b]
useWhen: Whether a linear system Ax = b has any solutions.

title: Cramer's rule
useWhen: Solving a square invertible system using determinants, one unknown at a time.

variables.meaning: A with column i replaced by the right-hand side

title: Taylor polynomial
useWhen: A polynomial that matches f and its derivatives at a chosen point a.

title: Lagrange remainder
useWhen: The error after replacing f by its Taylor polynomial of degree n.

variables.meaning: Some point between a and x

title: Maclaurin polynomial
useWhen: A Taylor polynomial expanded at 0, not at a general point a.

title: First-order homogeneous linear DE
useWhen: A first-order equation y' + a y = 0 with constant a.

title: Second-order homogeneous linear DE
katex: r^{2} + pr + q = 0 \text{ then } y \text{ from the roots } r
useWhen: A second-order equation y'' + p y' + q y = 0 with constant coefficients.

title: Current
useWhen: Charge passing a point in a circuit, per unit time.

title: Voltage
useWhen: Energy transferred per unit charge, or potential difference.

title: Resistance
useWhen: How much a component opposes current, from voltage and current.

title: Series circuit
katex: I_{\mathrm{tot}} = I_{1} = I_{2},\quad U_{\mathrm{tot}} = U_{1} + U_{2},\quad R_{\mathrm{tot}} = R_{1} + R_{2}
useWhen: Components on a single loop: same current, voltages add.

title: Parallel circuit
katex: I_{\mathrm{tot}} = I_{1} + I_{2},\quad U_{\mathrm{tot}} = U_{1} = U_{2},\quad \dfrac{1}{R_{\mathrm{tot}}} = \dfrac{1}{R_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{R_{2}}
useWhen: Components side by side: same voltage, currents add.

title: Electrical power
useWhen: The rate of electrical energy transfer from voltage and current.

title: Electrical energy
useWhen: Electrical energy from power and the time it runs.

title: Speed
useWhen: How fast something moves, from distance and time.

title: Acceleration from rest
katex: a = \dfrac{\Delta v}{\Delta t},\quad s = \dfrac{1}{2} a t^{2}
useWhen: Changing speed, or distance from rest under constant acceleration.

variables.meaning: Distance from rest under constant a

title: Weight
useWhen: The gravitational force on a mass near Earth.

title: Newton's second law
useWhen: The resultant force on a mass, or the acceleration it produces.

variables.meaning: Resultant force on a given mass

title: Frequency and period
useWhen: How often a cycle repeats, or the time for one cycle.

title: Wave speed
useWhen: How fast a wave travels, from frequency and wavelength.

title: Mechanical work
useWhen: Energy transferred by a force moving along its own direction.

title: Gravitational potential energy
useWhen: Energy stored by lifting a mass in a uniform gravitational field.

title: Kinetic energy
useWhen: Energy due to motion, from mass and speed.

title: Conservation of energy
useWhen: A closed system: total energy before equals total energy after.

variables.meaning: All forms of energy in the closed system

title: Heat to change temperature
useWhen: Heat that changes temperature, with no change of state.

title: Latent heat
useWhen: Heat that melts or boils a substance with no temperature change.

title: Momentum
useWhen: Mass times velocity, before looking at a collision.

title: Conservation of momentum
useWhen: A collision or explosion in a closed system, no external force.

title: Quantity after n half-lives
useWhen: How much of a radioactive sample remains after whole half-lives.

title: Mass–energy
useWhen: Energy equivalent to a change of mass, as in nuclear reactions.

title: Elementary charge
useWhen: The magnitude of the charge on a proton or electron.

variables.meaning: Magnitude of the charge on a proton or electron

title: Force between point charges
useWhen: The force between two point charges in a vacuum.

title: Electric field strength
useWhen: Force per unit charge on a small test charge.

title: Radial electric field
useWhen: The electric field around a single point charge, not parallel plates.

title: Uniform field between plates
useWhen: The field between parallel plates from voltage and separation.

title: Capacitor charge
useWhen: Charge stored on a capacitor from capacitance and voltage.

title: Energy stored in a capacitor
useWhen: The energy stored in a capacitor once it is charged.

title: Field inside a solenoid
useWhen: The uniform magnetic field inside a long solenoid.

title: Newton's law of gravitation
useWhen: The attractive force between two point masses, anywhere in space.

title: Gravitational field strength
useWhen: Gravitational force per unit mass on a test mass.

title: Radial gravitational field
useWhen: g due to a spherical mass, outside it, from GM/r^2.

title: Displacement against time
useWhen: Position against time when acceleration is constant, from s0 and v0.

title: Velocity against time
useWhen: Speed against time when acceleration is constant, from a starting v0.

title: Angular velocity
useWhen: How fast an angle changes, or linear speed on a circle.

title: Centripetal acceleration
useWhen: Acceleration toward the centre for uniform circular motion.

title: Angular frequency
useWhen: Oscillations: linking period, frequency and angular frequency omega.

title: Wave speed
useWhen: Speed of a progressive wave from frequency and wavelength.

title: SHM restoring force
useWhen: The restoring force toward equilibrium, proportional to displacement.

title: SHM acceleration
useWhen: Acceleration in SHM from omega and the displacement from equilibrium.

title: SHM displacement
useWhen: Position against time in SHM, from amplitude and omega.

title: Energy in an inductor
useWhen: Energy stored in an inductor's magnetic field, from L and I.

title: Natural frequency of an LC circuit
useWhen: The natural frequency of an undamped LC circuit.

title: Sinusoidal wave
useWhen: Displacement of a sinusoidal wave as a function of x and t.

title: Doppler effect — moving observer
useWhen: The heard frequency when the observer moves and the source is still.

title: Doppler effect — moving source
useWhen: The heard frequency when the source moves and the observer is still.

variables.meaning: Source speed; + when the source recedes

title: Reflection
useWhen: A wave bouncing off a boundary: angle in equals angle out.

title: Refraction (Snell)
useWhen: A wave changing speed as it crosses into another medium.

title: Young's double slit
useWhen: Fringe spacing from two slits, wavelength, and screen distance.

title: Grating formula
useWhen: Bright spots from a diffraction grating, order n.

title: Standing wave on a string
useWhen: A standing wave with the same condition at both ends.

variables.meaning: Length; also a pipe open or closed at both ends

title: Standing wave in a closed pipe
useWhen: A standing wave in a pipe with one end open and one closed.

variables.meaning: Length of a pipe with different ends

title: Electric potential difference
useWhen: Change in electrical potential energy per unit charge.

title: Potential of a point charge
useWhen: Electrical potential around a point charge, zero at infinity.

title: Work on a charge in a uniform field
useWhen: Work to move a charge through a potential difference.

title: Force on a current-carrying wire
useWhen: The force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field.

variables.meaning: Angle between the wire and B

title: Lorentz force
useWhen: The force on a moving charge in a magnetic field.

title: Magnetic flux
useWhen: How much magnetic field passes through an area.

variables.meaning: Component of B normal to the area

title: Electromagnetic induction
useWhen: An induced emf from a magnetic flux that is changing.

title: Gravitational potential difference
useWhen: Change in gravitational potential energy per unit mass.

title: Gravitational potential (radial)
useWhen: Gravitational potential around a point mass, zero at infinity.

title: Change of GPE in a uniform field
useWhen: Change of gravitational potential energy in a uniform field, mgΔh.

title: Energy of a photon
useWhen: The energy of a photon from its frequency, not its momentum.

title: Einstein's equation
useWhen: Maximum kinetic energy of a photoelectron from hf and the work function.

variables.meaning: Maximum kinetic energy of a photoelectron

title: Momentum of a photon
useWhen: The momentum of a photon from its wavelength, not of a particle.

title: de Broglie wavelength
useWhen: The wavelength associated with a moving particle, not a photon.

title: Uncertainty — position and momentum
useWhen: A lower bound on how well position and momentum can be known together.

title: Uncertainty — energy and time
useWhen: A lower bound on how well energy and time can be known together.

title: Infinite square well
useWhen: Allowed energies of a particle trapped in a 1D infinite well.

title: Hydrogen energy levels
useWhen: The energy of a hydrogen atom in level n.

title: Emission and absorption
useWhen: A photon emitted or absorbed when an electron jumps between levels.
